articles.title: Two Police Personnel Attacked by intoxicated men While Stopping Fight in Doddaballapur
articles.content: Vinod M Jain Bengaluru: Two police personnel attached to the 112 emergency response team were allegedly assaulted by two intoxicated men while trying to stop a fight at Palanajogihalli in Doddaballapur of Bengaluru Rural district. https://www.countryandpolitics.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/1003259946.mp4 The incident occurred when the personnel,identified as Manikantha and Rayappa Poojari,were on night patrol duty.Police received an alert through the 112 emergency helpline about two men fighting in the area. The officers reached the spot and found Harahan Sarihan and Basir alias Gidda allegedly quarrelling with each other.Both were reportedly under the influence of alcohol. When the personnel intervened to pacify them,the duo allegedly became aggressive and turned on the officers. The accused allegedly assaulted Manikantha and Rayappa Poojari,injuring them on their chest,hands and legs. The injured personnel were taken to Doddaballapur Government Hospital,where they received treatment. The Doddaballapur Rural police took both accused into custody shortly after the incident.Police are questioning them to ascertain the sequence of events and the circumstances leading to the alleged assault.Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: 'Love Always': Teaser of India's first Korean webtoon adaptation out - DT Next
articles.content: CHENNAI: JioHotstar has unveiled the teaser of its upcoming Tamil original series Love Always, which is set to stream from October 30. Directed by Madhumita, the eight-episode series marks what the makers describe as India’s first adaptation of a Korean webtoon. Produced by Kross Pictures and Guru Films, the series is based on the Korean webtoon Here We Go Again , created by Goeun and published on Kakao between 2015 and 2017. The story follows a married couple whose relationship has reached a breaking point. As they consider divorce, a magical twist turns them young again, giving them an unexpected opportunity to revisit their choices and relationship, and wonder what their future might look like. The Tamil adaptation features Gouri G Kishan, Ramzan Muhammed, Jayaprakash, Jayasudha and Maya Krishnan in key roles. Love Always will comprise eight episodes, with each episode running for around 30 minutes. The format is designed to combine the quick pace and visual storytelling associated with webtoons with the emotional elements of a family drama. The series will stream in Tamil on JioHotstar, with dubbed versions available in Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Hindi, Marathi and Bengali from October 30.

articles.title: CreditNirvana Launches India's First Integrated AI Suite for Voice Co-Browsing and Agentic ...
articles.content: PRNewswire Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], October 6: CreditNirvana , a Perfios company focused on agentic AI-driven debt management, today introduced ORCA and CognifAI Assist, an integrated AI suite that helps lenders collect at 40% lower cost with a 30% higher connect rate, and complete 60-70% of collection journeys autonomously without any human intervention. As digital lending continues to accelerate, financial institutions face a persistent dual challenge of steep customer drop-off rates during complex onboarding processes like re-KYC and loan origination, paired with escalating debt collection costs caused by rigid, repetitive outreach strategies. Overcoming these hurdles has historically required costly, time-consuming core infrastructure overhauls that slow down innovation and strain operational margins. CreditNirvana resolves this through a non-intrusive agentic AI layer that can be easily deployed over existing banking portals, mobile applications, and third-party systems without requiring core-system overhauls. CognifAI and ORCA function as AI solutions within CreditNirvana's broader agentic portfolio, operating with its flagship debt collection platform, Maestro, to deliver targeted automation across distinct stages of the credit lifecycle. Unlike conventional collections platforms that rely on predefined sequences of calls, messages and follow-ups, ORCA uses an agentic, contextualised and closed-loop approach to decide the next best action for each account, execute it, observe outcomes and adapt subsequent strategies. Powered by more than 200 specialised AI agents, ORCA coordinates collections across digital, voice, calling, field and legal touchpoints. Lenders define recovery objectives and constraints, while ORCA determines account-level strategies within lender-defined compliance guardrails and with human-in-the-loop control. Vinay Sathyanarayan, CEO of CreditNirvana, said, "The future of lending lies in making every customer interaction more contextual, efficient and seamless. With CognifAI and ORCA, we are extending the agentic AI layer across the lending lifecycle, from helping customers navigate digital journeys to enabling lenders to make more informed, account-level collections decisions leading to better collection strategy. Our focus is on combining measurable business outcomes with responsible AI deployment, customer experience and compliance guardrails." ORCA's measurement framework incorporates baselines, controls and outcome attribution. Its four interconnected layers - Signals, Decision, Execution and Measurement, continuously assess borrower behaviour, delinquency, promise-keeping and channel response, real time financial data to strategize collections decisions. Complementing ORCA, CognifAI combines an AI voice assistant capable of conversing across multiple Indian regional languages as well as global languages including Spanish, Mandarin, Arabic, and Bahasa, with secure visual co-browsing to guide customers screen-by-screen through digital lending, origination, and servicing journeys. Operating as an overlay requiring no app downloads, it highlights fields, pre-fills data, and supports in-session rate and tenure negotiations within approved guardrails. To protect sensitive customer information, CognifAI incorporates end-to-end encryption and field-level data masking for PAN, OTP, and account data, enabling lenders to achieve 30% higher journey completion and 35% lower handling time. Together, CognifAI and ORCA extend AI-led assistance and automation across customer acquisition, onboarding, servicing and collections. Built on CreditNirvana's enterprise-grade architecture, the platform currently orchestrates over $30 billion in Assets Under Management (AUM) across 100+ million loan accounts. articles.title: Rajnath Singh Launches India's First Indigenous Fleet Support Ship Surya In ... - Free Press Journal
articles.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday launched ‘Surya’, India’s first indigenous fleet support ship, at Hindustan Shipyard Ltd (HSL) in Visakhapatnam, marking a major step in the Navy’s efforts to strengthen its reach and endurance at sea. ‘Surya’ is the first of five fleet support ships being built at a cost of ₹19,000 crore. A warship’s launch is a significant stage in its construction as it marks the vessel entering the water for the first time. Navy Chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan was present at the event. A Bigger Maritime Ambition “India needs strong maritime capability. Our goal is to go beyond self-reliance and become a global maritime power,” Singh said. The launch underlines India’s growing focus on building critical naval platforms at home. More importantly, the fleet support ships will help the Navy remain at sea for longer periods, an increasingly important capability as its fleet expands and its responsibilities in the Indian Ocean region grow. Singh also laid the keel of another fleet support ship and inaugurated an upgraded slipway and a 300-tonne crane at the public sector shipyard. The Defence Ministry said the infrastructure would strengthen HSL’s capacity to build larger and more complex vessels while supporting India’s maritime capabilities. Keeping Warships At Sea Longer HSL is expected to deliver ‘Surya’ to the Navy next year, while the remaining vessels are expected to follow at the rate of one every 10 months. The fleet support vessels will be 225 metres long and 32 metres wide. They will replenish warships at sea with fuel, water, ammunition and stores, allowing the naval fleet to operate for prolonged periods without returning to harbour. “The launch of FSS-1 (Surya) is a symbol of achievement, keel laying of FSS-5 is a symbol of resolve and the new slipway is a symbol of our growing capability… Our goal should be to design better, build faster, and deliver on time,” Singh said. Expanding Fleet Needs More Support The Navy currently operates four fleet support vessels commissioned between 1996 and 2011. It needs additional support ships as its fleet expands and its roles and responsibilities in the Indian Ocean region increase. The five new vessels are therefore more than an addition to the Navy’s numbers. Their ability to replenish ships at sea can give the fleet greater operational flexibility and reduce the need for warships to frequently return to harbour for essential supplies. “Self-reliance is an important milestone, but global competitiveness is the next big leap,” Singh said, stressing that Indian shipyards must meet global benchmarks in quality, cost, technology, delivery and reliability, Hindustan Times reports. The Navy is working towards achieving full self-reliance by 2047, when India completes 100 years of independence. articles.title: India's first indigenous HPV vaccine gets WHO prequalification - Morung Express
articles.content: India’s first indigenous HPV vaccine gets WHO prequalification (Image credit: WHO/Representational) Health 6th October 2026 New Delhi, October 6 (IANS): Cervavac -- India's first indigenously developed human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine -- has received prequalification from the World Health Organization (WHO) which makes it eligible for procurement by United Nations agencies and expands its potential global reach. The vaccine -- which was developed by the Serum Institute of India (SII) -- had earlier received approval from India's Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) for domestic use. Cervavac is a quadrivalent, gender-neutral vaccine that can be administered to both girls and boys between the ages of nine and 26 years. It targets four HPV strains -- types 6, 11, 16 and 18. While HPV types 6 and 11 are commonly associated with genital warts, types 16 and 18 are considered high-risk strains linked to several cancers. In women, the vaccine helps protect against cervical, vulvar, vaginal and anal cancers associated with HPV infection. On the other hand, in men, it provides protection against HPV-related anal cancer. According to SII, children aged 9-14 years should receive two doses administered six months apart, while individuals aged 15-26 years require a three-dose schedule within a year. Commenting on the development, Serum Institute Chief Executive Officer Adar Poonawalla said the WHO prequalification marks an important step in strengthening the global fight against HPV-related diseases and broadening access to preventive vaccination. The vaccine contains proteins designed to generate an immune response against the four targeted HPV strains and is manufactured using the Hansenula polymorpha expression system. WHO prequalification is a key benchmark for vaccine quality, safety and efficacy and allows international agencies and global immunisation programmes to procure the product. Cervavac was developed by SII in partnership with the Department of Biotechnology, Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), WHO's International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) and the Gates Foundation.

articles.title: Quick Heal Foundation launches Cyber Shikshit | VARINDIA
articles.content: 6 October 2026 4 min read 0 views Share: f 𝕏 in The flagship initiative under ‘Cyber Shiksha, Cyber Suraksha’ programme will work towards making the entire village cyber safe through awareness, household outreach and hands-on digital security interventions Quick Heal Foundation, the CSR arm of Quick Heal Technologies Limited, a global provider of cybersecurity solutions, has launched its Cyber Shikshit Gaon initiative in Arjuni Village, Kolhapur, with the aim of making it India’s first cyber-safe village. As part of Quick Heal Foundation’s flagship Cyber Shiksha, Cyber Suraksha programme, the initiative takes a community-wide approach to cybersecurity, bringing together structured awareness sessions, household outreach and hands-on digital security interventions to equip residents with the knowledge and confidence to prevent, identify and report cyber threats. As digital access expands, awareness of online risks has not kept pace. People may unknowingly expose personal information through third-party applications, unknown platforms, excessive app permissions and unverified links. Such exposure can put not only an individual at risk, but also family members, friends and business contacts connected through their device. Built on three core pillars - Prevention, Protection and Reporting - the Cyber Shikshit Gaon initiative goes beyond conventional awareness to deliver hands-on digital protection and establish a sustainable village-level response ecosystem. Anupama Katkar, Chairperson, Quick Heal Foundation and Chief of Operational Excellence, Quick Heal Technologies Limited, said, “Digital access can open doors to opportunity, but those doors can only truly empower communities when people have the knowledge and confidence to stay safe online. Through Cyber Shikshit Gaon, we want to take cybersecurity beyond awareness and make it a part of everyday life, helping people protect their personal information, recognise fraud, secure their devices, and know where to turn when they need help. Arjuni is more than a village where we are taking this initiative; it is a reminder that every citizen, regardless of where they live, deserves the confidence to participate safely in the digital world. If we can help even one family feel safer online, we are taking one more meaningful step towards a truly cyber-resilient India.” Arjuni has an estimated population of 1,406. A baseline survey covered 273 households and identified 675 mobile users, including 539 smartphone users. Among the households surveyed, 193 reported daily internet use, while 155 reported regular or occasional UPI use, highlighting the need to strengthen cyber literacy alongside digital adoption. Further assessments in the village identified devices with security gaps and sensitive data exposure without users’ knowledge. Awareness of the critical first three hours - the ‘golden window’ for reporting financial cyber fraud - was also limited, reducing the possibility of timely intervention and recovery. The Cyber Shikshit Gaon is aimed at addressing these gaps. At the heart of the programme are members of the Cyber Warrior Club at Devchand College, Arjuni, working under the guidance of Quick Heal Foundation. These young volunteers are conducting household outreach and structured awareness sessions, while helping residents apply essential security measures to their devices and accounts. articles.title: Pune Ergonomics Centre to Build Safer Indian Designs - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Pune to Build India’s First Centre for Safer Human-Centred Design Breaking News Pune to Build India’s First Centre for Safer Human-Centred Design By Urban Acres October 6, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Pune will host India’s first Advanced Ergonomics and Human Factors Research Centre, a Rs 105-crore facility being established by the Automotive Research Association of India and COEP Technological University to develop design standards based on Indian body dimensions and usage conditions. The centre will be located at COEP Tech’s Research and Innovation Park in Chikhali and will be spread across 38,000 square feet. According to an official notification from ARAI, its first phase is planned over the next two to three years and will focus on establishing and upgrading facilities for posture evaluation, seating comfort analysis, human biomechanics and field-of-vision assessment. A second phase, expected to take another four to five years, will lead to the development of a full-scale Advanced Ergonomics and Human Factors Research Centre. The project will receive funding from industry stakeholders, government bodies and ministries, industry partners, corporate social responsibility initiatives and other institutions, the notification said. The initiative addresses a gap in product testing and design, according to ARAI senior deputy director Rahul Mahajan. He said Indian users differ from European populations in body dimensions, proportions and other physical characteristics, meaning that ergonomics standards, comfort criteria and testing protocols based on European datasets may not accurately represent Indian users or operating conditions. The implications extend beyond vehicle seats and workstations. The proposed centre is expected to support research and testing for automotive products, defence equipment, aerospace systems, railways, agricultural machinery, industrial equipment, consumer products, furniture, construction and built environments, and textiles. Mahajan said the differences also involve how products are used in India, including driving patterns, road environments and climatic conditions. The proposed centre will therefore work towards creating Indian anthropometric databases, standards, design methods and validation protocols for products intended to be safer and more comfortable for local users. For the built environment, the facility could provide a research base for examining how people interact with furniture, workstations, construction equipment and other spaces or products used in daily life. However, the project’s immediate scope and the specific standards it will eventually produce will depend on the research facilities developed during its two-phase implementation. The announcement places Pune at the centre of an effort to link academic research, automotive testing and industrial design. ARAI and COEP Tech are jointly establishing the facility, while additional government, industry and institutional funding is expected to support its development. The first milestone is the creation and upgrading of the specialised testing facilities during the initial two-to-three-year phase. articles.title: India Moves to Boost Navy's Endurance With Indigenous Fleet Support Ships - Bharatshakti
articles.content: Latest Latest News Rajnath Singh launches first Fleet Support Ship- 'FSS-1 Surya' at HSL as India expands capacity to build larger vessels India is moving to strengthen the Indian Navy’s ability to sustain prolonged operations far from its home ports with the launch of the country’s first indigenous Fleet Support Ship (FSS), a capability that will be increasingly important as the Navy seeks to maintain a persistent presence across the Indian Ocean Region. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh launched first Fleet Support Ship (FSS-1) named ‘Surya’ , at Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday. He also laid the keel of the fifth ship in the programme and inaugurated an upgraded shipbuilding slipway and a 300-tonne Goliath Crane. The three developments underline a larger objective: building not only more ships for the Navy but also the industrial capacity to construct increasingly large and complex vessels in India. “The launch of FSS-1 is a symbol of achievement, the keel laying of FSS-5 is a symbol of resolve and the new Slipway is a symbol of our growing capability,” Singh said. Enabling longer naval deployments Fleet Support Ships are a critical component of a blue-water navy. Unlike frontline warships, their primary role is to keep the fleet supplied and operational at sea through replenishment of fuel, water, ammunition, stores and other essential supplies. For the Indian Navy, which is increasingly operating across the wider Indian Ocean and maintaining deployments in distant waters, such vessels can reduce dependence on shore-based support and enable task groups to remain at sea for longer periods. The FSS programme is therefore aimed at strengthening the Navy’s reach, endurance and operational flexibility. Built indigenously by HSL, Surya and its sister ships will feature enhanced cargo and fluid capacity, first-line maintenance workshops and a helicopter deck capable of supporting multi-role helicopters. The vessels will also have self-defence systems. The launch of the first ship and keel laying of the fifth indicate that the programme is progressing simultaneously on construction and production lines. HSL prepares for larger ships The FSS milestone comes alongside a significant expansion of HSL’s shipbuilding infrastructure. The upgraded Slipway-4 has been extended and strengthened to enable the shipyard to build and launch vessels of up to 45,000 deadweight tonnes. A new 300-tonne Goliath Crane, spanning Slipways 3 and 4, is designed to handle heavier ship blocks and support modern block-construction techniques. Manufactured by L&T Geostructure with Konecranes under the Make in India initiative, the crane incorporates automated controls, variable-frequency drives, tandem lifting, remote diagnostics and condition monitoring. The infrastructure upgrade is intended to allow HSL to take on larger and more complex shipbuilding programmes. For the Indian shipbuilding sector, the significance extends beyond a single naval programme. The ability to construct large hulls, handle heavier blocks and improve construction timelines will be critical if Indian yards are to meet the Navy’s expanding requirements while also competing for international orders. articles.title: AI Rollouts Are Not Failing on Technology . The Real Bottleneck Is Human Behaviour
articles.content: As enterprises move from AI pilots to large-scale deployment, behavioural friction among employees and middle management could emerge as one of the biggest barriers to successful AI adoption, says Terragni Consulting Organisations are investing heavily in artificial intelligence platforms, pilots and employee training, but the biggest challenge in scaling AI may not lie in the technology itself. It may lie in whether people are willing and able to change the way they work. According to Terragni Consulting, the human behaviour and engagement-focused consulting firm, organisations often treat AI rollout as a technology deployment exercise, with training and successful pilots being viewed as indicators of adoption readiness. However, the transition from a successful pilot to enterprise-wide adoption can expose a less visible challenge — behavioural friction. “AI transformation is fundamentally behavioural” is the central proposition behind Terragni’s latest AI adoption framework, Vector, which looks at the human factors that can slow down AI adoption inside organisations. The issue, the firm argues, is that resistance to AI rarely appears as outright rejection. Instead, it can manifest through delayed approvals, pilot fatigue, over-governance, repeated escalation, excessive validation and performative compliance. By the time such resistance becomes operationally visible, adoption may already have slowed. The middle-management paradox One of the critical areas identified by Terragni is middle management. Middle managers play a crucial role in translating organisational strategy into execution, shaping team behaviour, determining how quickly new processes are adopted and creating the environment in which employees experiment with new technologies. At the same time, AI can potentially challenge the very structures around which middle-management roles have traditionally been built — including authority, expertise, control and relevance. This creates what Terragni describes as a “middle-management paradox”: the people expected to accelerate AI adoption may themselves experience uncertainty about what AI means for their role and influence. As a result, resistance may become psychological before becoming operational. Three hidden frictions behind AI adoption Terragni’s framework identifies three broad forms of friction that can influence whether employees embrace new AI-enabled ways of working. Cognitive friction: Employees may not fully understand how AI changes their role or responsibilities. Identity friction: Employees may question what happens to their expertise, value or professional identity if AI performs parts of their work faster. Context friction: Even when employees are willing to change, organisational systems, incentives and workflows may continue rewarding established behaviour. Together, these factors can create a gap between AI availability and actual AI adoption. From technology readiness to behavioural readiness Terragni’s approach proposes that organisations should assess behavioural readiness alongside technological readiness. Its Vector Solution Framework is structured around three stages — Diagnose, Map and Accelerate. The first stage identifies behavioural barriers such as readiness, managerial resistance, workflow friction, adoption anxiety, role ambiguity and incentive misalignment. The second maps these issues through tools such as AI readiness heatmaps, behavioural risk dashboards, resistance maps and adoption archetypes. The final stage prioritises interventions designed to make AI adoption more measurable, actionable and trackable. The approach is particularly relevant for organisations...

articles.title: Airtel Business launches India's first telco-grade network - Bisinfotech
articles.content: Airtel Business, India’s leading provider of secure and reliable connectivity, technology, and communications solutions, launched Airtel IQ Gateway, India’s first ever telco-grade network intelligence platform which brings different customer communication channels onto one safe control plane. Enterprises now won’t need to manage multiple vendors separately if they opt for Airtel IQ Gateway, a DPDP-compliant platform which combines SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, voice communications and number verification (silent authentication) together in one place. It will enable enterprises to easily manage their business communications at scale, while protecting customer trust and making safety foundational to every customer interaction. This offering from Airtel Business is of critical importance today, when businesses have to manage fragmented customer communication stacks across multiple service providers and tools to reach their customers, with limited visibility into the real delivery of messages. Messages are often reported delivered even when they fail, while International OTP pumping by bots inflates bills. Moreover, managing pre-approved message templates is manual and often leads to mistakes. For enterprises, especially in sectors like BFSI, government, e‑commerce and logistics, this not only hurts customer trust when consumers are targeted by scams, this also damages their brand reputation. Airtel IQ Gateway solves this with a single control center for all business communications. It brings together Airtel’s fraud protection with automatic integrations of native message template system (DLT), automatic switching to back-up service providers, and intelligent routing across SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice. Launched nationwide today after successful trial deployments across select banks, financial institutions and other relevant industry collaborations, the platform extends Airtel’s proven expertise in fraud prevention for end customers to enterprises, enabling them to build customer trust at scale through safe communications. articles.content: BULLET Microdrama, the platform backed by ZEE Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. (‘Z’), is expanding its content slate with the rollout of 100+ AI-powered microdramas , with Do Deewane aur Ashiqui as the first title to go live. The initiative brings together BULLET’s production partners and Trinetra AI - India’s first one of its kind AI-native filmmaking and content intelligence platform to build a larger pipeline of short-form, vertical and creator-driven stories for mobile-first audiences. The slate builds on BULLET’s focus on scaling the microdrama format while giving creators greater flexibility to experiment with new narratives, genres and story worlds. The story of Do Deewane Aashiqui follows Aditya, a young man who despises the wealthy after a powerful family causes his brother’s life to unravel. He falls for Ruhi, unaware that she is the daughter of the very businessman he holds responsible. As Ruhi hides her identity, their love grows, but when Aditya discovers the truth, he must choose between his love for her and his deep-rooted hatred for the world she comes from. To bring the wider slate of 100+ titles to audiences, BULLET Microdrama has partnered with multiple creative agencies like The Dosa Studios, The Filmy Musketeers Studio, FrameFry Studios, De Works Communications, SQB Pictures, Rajtaru Studio Limited and JVD Films. The partnership includes microdramas being developed end-to-end using BULLET’s Trinetra AI platform. The platform supports creators across multiple stages of the filmmaking process, from story development and visualisation to production. Trinetra AI’s script intelligence arm, Trishul, evaluates scripts across 100+ parameters to identify story strength and regional fit, while Rudra, the neural narrative generation engine supports storyboarding, character and universe creation, shot breakdown and video generation. Its audio orchestration model, Damrooh, takes care of dialect-accurate dialogues and background music. The slate also explores story worlds and genres that can be complex or expensive to execute through conventional production. Set against distinctive backdrops, including underwater and superhero universes, these titles demonstrate the creative range of AI-enabled production across different storytelling environments. For a format built around 60–100 high-hook episodes, AI enables greater production speed and scale while giving creators more room to experiment with stories, worlds and formats. It also expands the ecosystem to AI artists and creative talent beyond traditional production hubs, with BULLET positioning AI as a complement to, rather than a replacement for live-action production. Azim Lalani, Co-Founder & Chief Business Officer, BULLET Microdrama , said, “AI is beginning to change the economics of content, not simply by making production cheaper, but by changing how BULLET Microdrama decides where to place its bets. There is immense opportunity in building a tighter feedback loop between what is written, what is produced and what audiences actually respond to. For microdrama, where creators are constantly testing new narratives and formats, this marks a shift from learning afterwards to learning faster and making sharper choices. articles.title: HSL Vizag Launches India's First Indigenous Fleet Support Ship
articles.content: Team Yo! Vizag Visakhapatnam , News/City Updates 3 hours ago Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), Vizag, began as Scindia Shipyard in 1941, when industrialist Walchand Hirachand sought to build ships locally rather than rely on UK-built vessels. Dr Rajendra Prasad laid the foundation stone on June 21, 1941, and the shipyard’s landmark moment came on March 14, 1948, with the launch of SS Jala Usha, the first steamship built in the Indian subcontinent after World War II. In 85 years, HSL has progressed from producing a single steamship to indigenous warships, diving support vessels and Fleet Support Ships. Today, on 6 October 2026, the shipyard has entered a new chapter, as Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh made his maiden visit to mark three significant milestones: new capacity for ship-building, the launch of India’s first indigenous Fleet Support Ship, ‘Surya’, and a keel-laying for the next one. Over the past fifteen months, HSL has already been delivering one milestone after another. In July 2025, it commissioned INS Nistar, India’s first indigenously designed and built Diving Support Vessel, with over 80% indigenous content and capabilities not found in any previous naval Diving Support Vessel worldwide. On 30 August 2026, the second Diving Support Vessel, INS Nipun, joined the fleet, strengthening the Navy’s deep-sea diving and submarine rescue capability. The launch of three more breakthroughs today added to HSL’s proud achievements. These include an upgraded Slipway-4, supported by a 300-tonne Goliath Crane built under Make in India by M/s L&T Geostructure with Konecranes, which now enables the shipyard to build and launch ships of up to 45,000 DWT. FSS-1, named ‘Surya,’ the first of five Fleet Support Ships being built for the Indian Navy, is also entering the waters of the Bay of Bengal today, just 18 months after steel cutting. These 43,500-tonne vessels will replenish warships at sea, extending the Navy’s endurance and reach across the Indian Ocean Region. Lastly, the keel laying of FSS-5 then marked HSL’s steady march towards producing the rest of the ships in the series. Commenting on the latest developments, Rear Admiral C Raghuram, VSM (Retd.), Chairman & Managing Director, HSL, said, “Two warships commissioned, a record year and now three milestones in a single day. From our best-ever year to this historic day, every milestone reflects a shipyard rising to the nation’s call, and 6th October marks our next leap forward.” Speaking on the occasion, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said, “HSL is strengthening India’s maritime foundation as a national custodian of the country’s maritime capabilities. Together with the Naval Dockyard and the Port, it anchors Vizag’s maritime ecosystem, reflecting the expertise and engineering talent of our workforce. Fleet support will further advance our vision for the Indian Ocean, given its economic, energy and national security significance. From today, HSL must prepare for the Indian Navy’s requirements in the years ahead, while Vizag must prepare for the maritime industry India will need in the future.” Looking back at how far HSL has come, the contrast is striking. articles.title: Oolka, India's AI -Powered Credit Platform, Brings Credit Analysis, Dispute Management and ...
articles.content: PNN Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], October 6: Oolka, India’s AI-powered credit platform, brings credit analysis, dispute management and credit profile improvement together in a single app. The platform is now used by more than one crore Indians across 19,065 of the country’s roughly 19,100 pincodes, in all 36 states and union territories. For most borrowers, fixing a credit problem has meant working across several disconnected places. A score app shows the number. Disputes go through the credit bureau’s own process. NOCs and closure letters are chased separately with each lender. Conversations about settlement or restructuring happen over the phone, often with no written record. Oolka brings these steps into one place, and its AI credit assistant , Oolka AI, carries out much of the work itself. Credit analysis Oolka AI reads a user’s Experian credit report line by line and explains it in plain language, in more than 100 Indian languages. It identifies the specific entries weakening a user’s credit profile, such as repaid loans still showing as active, incorrect late-payment records, duplicate accounts and high credit card utilisation. Users do not need to know the terminology to ask. One in three Oolka users sends screenshots of financial documents and messages to have them explained, and 40 lakh messages have arrived as voice notes. Dispute management When Oolka AI finds an error, it acts on it. It files disputes and handles the follow-up communication with the credit bureau, drafts NOC and account-closure requests to lenders, and tracks each case until it is resolved. It keeps a record of every dispute, email and lender reply across the full history of a user’s case, so nobody has to start over or explain their situation twice. Credit profile improvement Beyond correcting errors, Oolka AI builds a personalised repayment plan that tackles the costliest debt first and reworks the order as loans close. It flags when card utilisation is too high, suggests consolidation where it lowers the total cost, and drafts restructuring, settlement and penalty-waiver requests to lenders. The improvements show up where lenders look first. More than 14,000 Oolka users now see their credit score rise in a typical week, three times the weekly figure in June. In one case, a school-van operator in Gurugram came to Oolka with a credit score that had stayed flat. Oolka AI traced the problem to his credit profile: a ₹5 overdue balance was keeping one account marked as active and overdue, holding back his entire file, and his card utilisation sat above 80%. Once the balance was cleared and his utilisation brought under control, his score began improving and he was approved for a consumer loan. “A credit score tells you something is wrong. It doesn’t tell you what’s wrong – or help you fix it. People came to Oolka not because they needed another credit score, but because they needed someone to read their report, find the problem, and get it resolved. That’s what we built Oolka to do.” “Our users are in almost every pincode...

articles.title: Pune To Host India's First Advanced Centre For Ergonomics And Human Factors Research
articles.content: Oct 06, 2026 | Updated 10:55 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . The Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and COEP Technological University will jointly set up the country's first Advanced Ergonomics and Human Factors Research Centre (AEHFRC) in Pune, with a planned investment of Rs 105 crore. The centre will come up at COEP Tech's Research and Innovation Park in Chikhali. It will develop engineering technologies and products built around the physical traits, needs and working conditions of Indian users. A Letter of Intent (LoI) was signed on 5 October in the presence of COEP Tech Vice-Chancellor Prof. Sunil Bhirud, ARAI Director Dr Reji Mathai and officials from both institutions. According to ARAI, the facility will span nearly 38,000 square feet. It aims to build domestic expertise in the field and reduce India's reliance on technologies largely designed for European users. In line with the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision, it will serve as a dedicated hub for research, testing, validation, training and innovation. The project will be executed in two phases. The first, spanning two to three years, will set up or upgrade facilities for posture evaluation, seating comfort analysis, human biomechanics and field-of-vision assessment. Over the following four to five years, the second phase will develop the AEHFRC into a full-fledged National Centre of Excellence. The centre will serve sectors including automotive, defence, aerospace, railways, agriculture, industrial equipment, consumer goods, furniture, construction and textiles. It will help industries assess how their products and systems interact with users in order to improve safety, efficiency and comfort. Its testing and validation support is expected to help companies address aspects such as vehicle seating, driver posture, visibility, workplace design and human-machine interaction early in product development. The centre will also offer specialised training and certification programmes. By linking academic research with industry needs, it aims to turn scientific findings into practical applications. articles.title: Airtel Business Unveils IQ Gateway: India's First Telco-Grade Enterprise Messaging Platform
articles.content: Airtel Business today launched Airtel IQ Gateway, India’s first ever telco-grade network intelligence platform which brings different customer communication channels onto one safe control plane. Enterprises now won’t need to manage multiple vendors separately if they opt for Airtel IQ Gateway, a DPDP-compliant platform which combines SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, voice communications and number verification (silent authentication) together in one place. It will enable enterprises to easily manage their business communications at scale, while protecting customer trust and making safety foundational to every customer interaction. This offering from Airtel Business is of critical importance today, when businesses have to manage fragmented customer communication stacks across multiple service providers and tools to reach their customers, with limited visibility into the real delivery of messages. Messages are often reported delivered even when they fail, while International OTP pumping by bots inflates bills. Moreover, managing pre-approved message templates is manual and often leads to mistakes. For enterprises, especially in sectors like BFSI, government, e‑commerce and logistics, this not only hurts customer trust when consumers are targeted by scams, this also damages their brand reputation. Airtel IQ Gateway solves this with a single control center for all business communications. It brings together Airtel’s fraud protection with automatic integrations of native message template system (DLT), automatic switching to back-up service providers, and intelligent routing across SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice. By leveraging Airtel’s built-in network intelligence and trust layers for enterprise use, such as IQ Verify for fraud protection and Silent Authentication for SIM based login, with capabilities like spotting fraudulent account creations and takeovers and artificial traffic spikes, Airtel IQ Gateway protects enterprises from fraud losses and billing spikes caused by industry-wide SMS pumping. Launched nationwide today after successful trial deployments across select banks, financial institutions and other relevant industry collaborations, the platform extends Airtel’s proven expertise in fraud prevention for end customers to enterprises, enabling them to build customer trust at scale through safe communications. Sharat Sinha, CEO – Airtel Business, said, “As India accelerates towards a safe, inclusive digital economy, trust must become the foundation of every digital interaction. Secure-by-design customer engagement is today the bedrock on which enterprises can scale with confidence. At Airtel, we have already demonstrated the power of network-grade fraud prevention in protecting millions of consumers across our mobile and digital services. With IQ Gateway, we are extending this proven expertise to enterprises, enabling them to build brand trust while ensuring every customer conversation is safe, authenticated and resilient. By embedding trust at the network layer, we are enabling our enterprise customers, especially banks, government departments and logistics firms, to reduce cybercrime losses and strengthen the credibility of every customer interaction. This is a decisive step towards a safer digital future for India, where citizens and businesses can transact and engage with equal confidence.” Key capabilities of Airtel IQ Gateway Flexible deployment: It can be integrated with existing communication workflows and vendor ecosystems.
